declarations.description:
Breadcrumb trail with overflow truncation.

Marina reference: `ds-breadcrumb` + `ds-breadcrumb-item` (chubb-design-system).
Marina renders two custom elements (a container plus one child element per
crumb); mms-breadcrumbs folds both into a single data-driven component —
consistent with a `items` array being the natural shape for a trail
(order and truncation are structural, not something a consumer composes
via light-DOM slotting the way `mms-checkbox-group` composes independent
`mms-checkbox` children).

Implementation notes (see DS-061 token mapping / PR notes for full detail):
- Renders the WAI-ARIA APG breadcrumb landmark (`nav[aria-label] > ol > li`)
  with `aria-current="page"` on the current crumb.
- No host-level `tabindex="0"` — the real interactive elements are the
  composed `mms-link` crumbs, each with their own tab stop and focus ring.
- The overflow ("…") crumb renders as static, non-interactive text — no
  overflow menu is implemented, so a focusable no-op control would be a
  keyboard trap with no purpose.
- Sub-item crumbs use `link-color="neutral"` (inherits surrounding text
  color), matching mms's own documented guidance for breadcrumbs/footers
  (see mms-link Overview story).
- `maxItems` governs the truncated count (`first + overflow +
  last(maxItems - 2)`, floored at 1 trailing item) — a prop named
  `maxItems` that doesn't control the rendered count would be misleading.
declarations.name: MmsBreadcrumbs

members.name: _stopNativeFocusEvent
members.description:
The trigger's own native `focus`/`blur` are `composed: true` and would cross
the shadow boundary, reaching a host listener alongside the CustomEvents
dispatched from `_handleFocusIn`/`_handleFocusOut` — firing a consumer's
`onFocus`/`onBlur` twice, with `e.detail` being the number 0 (UIEvent.detail)
on the native one. The declared `@fires focus` / `@fires blur` contract is the
CustomEvent; the native duplicate is leakage.

Only `focus`/`blur` are stopped. `focusin`/`focusout` still propagate out, as
they do from any ordinary element — a parent form or focus-tracking library
relies on that, and neither name collides with a declared event.

declarations.description:
Toast component for temporary, dismissible notifications.

Self-positions in a fixed, bottom-center viewport stack — no wrapper or manager element
required, the same self-positioning pattern as mms-modal. Width is 560px, centered, above
the mms 768px layout-padding-step; below it, the toast insets from both viewport edges
instead (`width: auto; left: 20px; right: 20px;`).

When more than one instance is connected, a shared registry (src/utils/toast-stack.ts)
tracks every mounted mms-toast and writes a `--_stack-offset` custom property onto each
host so they stack with a 12px gap instead of overlapping — newest-connected sits nearest
the bottom edge, older instances are pushed upward. Offsets recompute live via a
ResizeObserver, so message text wrapping re-flows the whole stack automatically.
z-index is 1100 — deliberately above mms-modal's 1000. A toast is a system-level, time-sensitive
message (e.g. a background save completing) that should reach the user regardless of what dialog
is open; it never traps or steals focus (aria-live announces without a focus change), so sitting
above the modal doesn't conflict with the modal's own focus trap (WCAG 2.4.3).
declarations.name: MmsToast

Same opt-in timer pattern as mms-alert-banner's `autoDismiss`/`autoDismissDuration` (pause on hover/focus, WCAG 2.2.1/2.2.2) — Marina's `ds-toast` JSDoc describes auto-dismiss but its actual implementation never started a timer; this is a real one.

declarations.description:
Contextual tooltip that reveals supplementary text next to a trigger icon
(or a custom slotted trigger). Ported from Marina's ds-tooltip; the
stroke/fill style split did not carry forward — mms has no inverse-surface
token yet, so the bubble uses the same elevated-surface treatment as
mms-select's dropdown and mms-modal (see token-strategy.md).
declarations.name: MmsTooltip

slots.description: Optional custom trigger content. Falls back to a question-mark icon.

members.name: text
members.description: Tooltip body text. Default 'Tooltip text'.

members.name: size
members.description: Text/padding scale: sm or md. Default 'md'. Max-width is a flat 240px regardless of size or viewport (Fluent UI's tooltip cap) — tooltip content is meant to be brief (Nielsen Norman Group), so no viewport-conditional clamp is needed.

members.name: direction
members.description: Bubble placement relative to trigger. Default 'below-right'. A placement hint, not a guarantee: on open, the bubble measures itself against the viewport and flips vertical (below/above) and/or horizontal (right/left) independently if the authored placement would clip — an mms addition with no Marina equivalent.

members.name: iconSize
members.description: Size of the default trigger icon: sm (16px) or lg (24px). Default 'sm'.

members.name: trigger
members.description: Interaction that reveals the bubble: hover, focus, or click. Default 'hover'.

members.name: active
members.description: Reflected state; true while the bubble is visible.

members.name: _effectiveDirection
members.description:
Effective placement actually applied to the bubble, reflected to the
`data-direction` host attribute the DIRECTION CSS block reads from.
Kept separate from `direction` (the public, author-set prop/attribute)
so viewport-collision flipping in _updatePosition() never mutates the
value a consumer set — only the rendered placement changes. Marina's
tooltip.component.ts (a reference starting point, not a spec) has no
equivalent logic — it always renders at the author-specified direction
with no collision handling; this is an mms-specific addition.

members.name: _handleFocusIn
members.description:
Gated on :focus-visible, not just focus — clicking .trigger (tabindex=0)
focuses it as a side effect, but the browser's own focus-visible heuristic
correctly excludes pointer-driven focus. Without this check, trigger="focus"
would open on mouse click too, indistinguishable from trigger="hover"/"click".

members.name: _updatePosition
members.description:
Viewport-edge collision handling — an mms addition with no Marina
equivalent (see _effectiveDirection doc above). Resets to the authored
`direction` on every open so repeated opens never compound a stale
flip, then measures `.tooltip-content` against the viewport on the next
frame and flips vertical (below/above) and/or horizontal (right/left)
independently if the authored placement would clip.

The flip math derives the *projected* rect for the opposite placement
from a single measurement rather than re-rendering and re-measuring:
.tooltip-content's width/height don't change with direction (only its
position does), and the vertical gap / horizontal arrow-offset are each
driven by one shared CSS custom property used symmetrically for both
sides of that axis (--_bubble-gap for below/above, --_arrow-offset-icon-*
for right/left) — so the observed offset on the current side is reused
unchanged to project the flipped side.

One-shot per open — doesn't re-verify the flipped placement also fits,
since a viewport too small for the bubble in every direction is out of
scope here.

members.name: _handleSlotChange
members.description:
Tracks whether a consumer has slotted custom trigger content, ported
from Marina's _handleSlotChange. Unlike Marina, mms uses this to
conditionally set aria-label on .trigger itself (see render()) — the
default icon's own label lives on mms-icon's internal shadow-DOM <svg>,
not its host, so it never reaches the ancestor's accessible-name
computation. Setting aria-label one level up on .trigger fixes that
without touching the shared mms-icon component, and is skipped when
custom content is slotted so we don't mask that content's own name.
